findings.title: Exit code 4 changes meaning from 'recreate upgrade' to 'feature disabled'
findings.body: RECREATE_UPGRADE_EXIT_CODE moves from 4 to 3, and 4 is reused for the new FEATURE_DISABLED code. Any script, pipeline or operator logic that treated exit code 4 as 'rolling upgrade not possible, recreate' now reads a disabled feature as a recreate result. Meanwhile 3 means recreate. Because the old and new meanings overlap on 4, a consumer that was not updated fails silently instead of loudly. The PR should check every consumer of these exit codes (operator code, tests, scripts) and call out the renumbering. The docs already listed 3, so the old code was out of sync with them, but the swap is still a contract change.

findings.title: Disabled-feature path is only tested for 'metadata' and the exit code is never asserted
findings.body: testFeatureNotEnabled only launches `update-compatibility metadata` and checks the error text. The `check` subcommand has the same new guard but no test. Neither test asserts that the process exits with CompatibilityResult.FEATURE_DISABLED (4), which is the contract the docs and scripts depend on. A regression that returned 0 or 1 with the same message would pass. Add a `check` case and assert the exit code.

findings.title: Macro hard-codes `--features=rolling-updates` and can clash with the user's own `--features`
findings.body: The guide tells users to pass the same options they use for `start`, but the macro now appends `--features=rolling-updates` to every update-compatibility example. A user who already sets `--features=...` for their deployment will either repeat the option, which may be rejected, or drop their other features from the compatibility run. The guide should say that `rolling-updates` must be added to the existing feature list instead of presenting it as part of the fixed command. Also, `features` is a build-time option, so a custom image must be built with it. The operator docs' new CAUTION says only that the Operator 'will fail' and does not say that.
